2.0.0.en: 1 Thus saith the LORD; "For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime: 2 But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kerioth: and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet: 3 And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all the princes thereof with him, saith the LORD."

2.0.1.en: In our study of the book of Ezekiel we saw that Moab descended from Lot by his elder daughter, and that he was called "Moab" because his mother bore him by her own father, since the word "Moab" means "from the father." St. Jerome sees that the elder daughter took advantage of her father's drunkenness and bore Moab by him, that he might point to Satan and to all who depart from God their Father and do not think of Him. St. Augustine sees that the sons of Moab point to whoever uses the Law in an unlawful, sinful manner, so that they stumble in it, just as Lot's daughter used her father in a sinful manner.

2.0.2.en: The crime of the sons of Moab is that they stole the bones of the king of Edom and burned them to turn them into lime. Although this seems a simple crime, God hates sin, however small its measure may be in our eyes. It is remarkable that the bones belonged to a king who was an enemy of the people of God, yet God does not love cruelty or violence, even when it is directed against dead enemies.

2.0.3.en: The fruit of this cruelty is that He returns the fire of their cruelty upon their most fortified city, "Kerioth," which was perhaps the capital of Moab (it is Khirbet al-Rabbah, 14 miles south of the river Arnon). He turns Moab into a war zone that dies at the sound of the trumpet, and He deprives it of the judge in its midst, so that there is neither justice nor wisdom in it, and He slays its princes.

2.0.4.en: What Moab did to the dead bones, with an evil soul and a hard heart, returns upon its cities, its princes and its people!

2.1.0.en: 4 Thus saith the LORD; "For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have despised the law of the LORD, and have not kept his commandments, and their lies caused them to err, after the which their fathers have walked: 5 But I will send a fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem."

2.1.1.en: If the word "Judah" means "confession," then those who ought to have declared their faith and confessed it through their obedience to the divine commandment are themselves the ones who "despised the law of the LORD, and have not kept his commandments, and their lies caused them to err, after the which their fathers have walked" [4]. Instead of confessing the truth, they accepted falsehood and walked after errors and lies!

2.1.2.en: What grieves the soul is that the fire turns back to burn the palaces of Jerusalem. If Jerusalem means "the vision of God," then turning away from God's commandment and running after errors corrupts the inner sight, so that it does not behold God. For this reason the Lord says: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God" (Mt 5:8). As St. Augustine says: [Let us purify our hearts by faith, that we may be made ready for Him who cannot be described, that is, for the unseen vision]. He also says: [All that the divine Holy Scriptures present aims only at purifying the inner sight, which hinders it from seeing God. Just as the eye was created to see this temporal light, so that if a foreign body enters it, it clouds its clearness and separates it from seeing that light, so also is the eye of your heart: if it is clouded and wounded, it turns away from the light of righteousness and does not dare or manage to look at it... And what clouds the clearness of the eye of your heart? Lust, covetousness, iniquity and worldly pleasure; all this clouds the eye of the heart, closes it and blinds it].

2.2.0.en: 6 Thus saith the LORD; "For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes; 7 That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and turn aside the way of the meek: and a man and his father will go in unto the same maid, to profane my holy name: 8 And they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. 9 Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath. 10 Also I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you forty years through the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite. 11 And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the LORD. 12 But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not. 13 Behold, I am pressed under you, as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves. 14 Therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not strengthen his force, neither shall the mighty deliver himself: 15 Neither shall he stand that handleth the bow; and he that is swift of foot shall not deliver himself: neither shall he that rideth the horse deliver himself. 16 And he that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day, saith the LORD."

2.2.1.en: Before presenting sermons to Israel, He revealed to them the secret of their chastisement, showing three matters:

2.2.3.en: Second: Their meeting God's kindnesses to them with ingratitude [9-12].

2.2.4.en: Third: All of them falling under chastisement [13-16].

2.3.0.en: "Thus saith the LORD; For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes" [6].

2.3.1.en: Perhaps this is the first written accusation that a prophet from among the "writing prophets" directs against Israel in the name of the Lord Himself: "they sold the righteous for silver." Who is this righteous one who was sold for silver but the Lord Christ, who alone is righteous, without sin, whom Judas the traitor sold for thirty pieces of silver, the price of a slave (Mt 27:5; Lk 22:5), He who bought us not with gold or silver, but with His precious blood? The Lord offered His life as a ransom for the slave, and the slave sold his Lord for silver, betraying Him. In bitterness the prophet Zechariah says: "So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them" (Zech 11:12-13). This is the goodly price at which the Lord was priced!

2.3.2.en: It is the sin of all generations: Israel sells the Lord for thirty pieces of silver, since the silver of the world rises in its eyes above life with the Lord, and it values temporal things above divine things!

2.3.3.en: What does the selling of the poor for a pair of shoes [6] also mean? Who is this needy one who is sold for a pair of shoes but the Lord Christ, who presents Himself to us through the suffering, the needy and the poor?! God asked His prophet Moses to take off his shoes, so that he might be able to enter into the divine holy things, behold the mysteries of God, enter with Him into a friendly conversation, and receive the pastoral work (Ex 3). For the same reason the Lord asked His disciples not to have shoes (Mt 10:10), so that they would not walk as earthly men who walk on the ground in shoes, but would lift their hearts up to heaven and draw with them, by the Holy Spirit, every heart to where Christ is seated. But man in his folly, instead of taking off his shoes to live in the heavens and to rise to the divine things, sells the poor man, "Christ Himself," for a pair of shoes, preferring rather to be bound to earthly things and to walk in temporal things, instead of being freed from shoes and living in heavenly things.

2.3.4.en: Origen sees in the shoes a reference to the dead temporal life and to the love of display. For shoes are made from the skin of dead animals, which is also used in drums that give out sounds without any work. Thus the Lord Christ, with His eternal glory, is sold for the sake of the dead temporal life, or for the acquiring of vain temporal honor that has a glittering appearance without serious inner work!

2.3.5.en: The Lord went on to reveal strange examples of the abominations that the Israelites were committing, in which uncleanness in its most hideous forms was mingled with injustice, namely:

2.4.0.en: A. "That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor" [7], and in some translations, "they trample the head of the poor down to the dust of the earth!" Not only do they show no pity to their poor brethren, but in the coarseness of their hearts they wrong them, dragging their heads down to the dust in order to tread on them with their feet.

2.4.1.en: Who is this head of the poor on whom they tread with their feet but the Lord Christ Himself, the Head of the whole Church? They despise Him and make light of His precious salvation. As the Apostle Paul says: "Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?" (Heb 10:29).

2.4.2.en: When we despise the poor man and treat him lightly, we are only despising his Head, Christ Jesus Himself. For this reason St. John Chrysostom says: [How great is the rank of the poor, for they are like the chamber of God, in which the righteous One is hidden! The poor man stretches out his hand begging, but it is God who receives your alms]. He also says in the person of the Lord: [It has reached you about Me that I am clothed with light as with a garment, but when you clothe a naked man I feel warmth and I am covered!].

2.4.3.en: B. "And turn aside the way of the meek" [7], that is, they close the road before the suffering... They do not stop at passivity, that is, ignoring the needy and sorrowful man, but if they find an open road before him for his salvation, they close it. They are volunteers working for the kingdom of injustice.

2.4.4.en: C. "And a man and his father will go in unto the same maid, to profane my holy name" [7]. It is a hideous picture of abominations that a man and his father should share in the sin of fornication with one young maiden! As St. Basil the Great says in his letter to Diodorius: [The Law never mentioned a man and his father committing fornication with a young maiden, because it is a hideous matter that needs no warning against, just as the Apostle Paul said: "But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints" (Eph 5:3)].

2.5.0.en: D. "And they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god" [8]. The matter does not stop at their staying by the pagan altars and sharing in the feasts of the house of the strange gods; rather, this abominable work was mingled with cruelty. While they pretend piety as they lie down beside every altar, behold they lie down upon the clothes of the poor, who pledged them with them and were unable to pay the amount and receive back the clothes, and they drink the wine of those who have financial fines and are unable to pay what is owed by them!! They worship using the clothes and wine of the poor who are unable to obtain the basic necessities of life!

2.6.s.en: Second: Their meeting God's kindnesses to them with ingratitude [9-12]:

2.6.0.en: Having listed bitter pictures and examples of the abominations of the Israelites, mingled with injustice and cruelty, He wished to affirm that they are without excuse, since God had shown them many kindnesses, and instead of repaying them with a holy and gentle life, behold, they walk in ingratitude.

2.6.1.en: "Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath. Also I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you forty years through the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite. And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the LORD. But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not" [9-12].

2.6.2.en: It is the constant story of man: in every generation God offers salvation, declaring His surpassing divine love for man, and man in the folly of his heart meets love with ingratitude!

2.6.3.en: From the historical side, God prepared the way for Israel of old. Since the Amorites were giants like the cedar and strong like the oak, God broke their fruit and uprooted their roots from the depths, and set out with His people from the land of Egypt, carried as if on the wings of His surpassing love, caring for them throughout their stay in the wilderness for forty years, until He delivered to them the land of the Amorites. And the sign of His love for them is that He made prophets for Himself from among them, and from their young men Nazarites consecrated in His name! But they met love with hatred, and God's gifts with ingratitude and disobedience. The sign of this is that they asked the Nazarites to drink wine, and commanded the prophets not to utter a word of the Lord. As St. John Chrysostom says: [God accused the Israelites, showing that they deserve a greater chastisement because they sinned after He had granted them such great honors].

2.6.4.en: It is remarkable that He put the giving of wine to the Nazarites before their commanding the prophets not to utter the word of the Lord and His prophecies, because drinking wine signifies man's loss of his balance and wisdom, so that he serves the house of the Lord in a state of drunkenness, which corrupts the house of God and destroys its peace. As St. Jerome says: [Aaron and the other priests used to abstain from every strong drink when they entered the temple, lest they die. This teaches us that those who serve in the Church without reverence die]. If compelling the prophets to stop bearing witness to God by proclaiming the word of prophecy is a grave sin, how much more so for one who enters the house of God and not only stands silent about the truth, but in irreverence confuses the truth, corrupts the sanctuary of God and hinders the spiritual work.

2.6.5.en: Let us return once more to God's work with Israel, to see His work with each one of us. The Amorite whom He destroyed before us is none other than the enemy of good, the devil, who ruled the earth for a time. He appeared like a giant like the cedar and strong like the oak, so we feared him and dreaded him, but the Lord by His cross broke his authority, and by the preaching of Him He saw him fallen from heaven like lightning (Lk 10:18). The Lord brought us up, as it were, from the land of bondage, carrying us by His Holy Spirit to inherit the land that the Amorite had ruled for a time, so that we became kings and priests to the Lord. May we not do what the Israelites did, drinking of the wine of the world and ceasing from the spirit of prophecy, or witness, for the Lord.

2.7.s.en: Third: All of them falling under chastisement [13-16]:

2.7.0.en: The Lord affirms that, since they sinned, there is no possibility of escaping chastisement, and He began His speech by saying: "Behold, I am pressed under you, as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves" [13]. In many translations: "Behold, I press from under you, as the full cart presses." It is as though God complains of the weight of our sins, which press upon Him, as though we were a cart full of sheaves.

2.7.1.en: God, who upholds the whole world by the word of His power, groans because of our sins and iniquities! He says: "I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting. Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them" (Isa 1:13-14). Again, when He sees His people turning back from Him, He says in bitterness: "Mine heart is turned within me" (Hos 11:8).

2.7.2.en: May we not be like the cart full of sheaves of evil, which weighs upon the soul and heart of our heavenly Father and presses upon our Redeemer who said: "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death... O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me" (Mt 26:38-39). Rather, let us be God's chariot of fire, bearing His heavenly nature working in us, so that we do not represent a weight and pressure upon Him, but fly by the Spirit of the Holy God, soaring in the heavenly places, rising from glory to glory without hindrance!

2.7.3.en: Instead of being a cart burdened with sheaves of evil, hindering God's saving work, may we be like a light, swift cloud carrying the Lord who rides upon it, heading toward Egypt to set up an altar for Himself in the midst of it (Isa 19).

2.7.4.en: The Lord continues His speech: "Therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not strengthen his force, neither shall the mighty deliver himself: Neither shall he stand that handleth the bow; and he that is swift of foot shall not deliver himself: neither shall he that rideth the horse deliver himself. And he that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day, saith the LORD" [14-19].

2.7.5.en: What a harsh and difficult picture! No one, however great his wisdom and abilities, can escape chastisement. "The flight shall perish from the swift," that is, the refuge or escape flees from him who thinks himself quick-witted and able to run away. For at that time, when man falls under the fruit of his sins, his intellectual ability to act (swiftly) at that time does not rescue him, nor does the strength of the body strengthen him, nor the heroism for which he was famous, nor the bow in his hands, nor the horse he rides, nor the strength of heart for which he was known... He cannot be saved, but stands naked, because he is found not clothed with "Christ," our righteousness!

2.7.6.en: May we possess "Christ Jesus" our Lord within us. He alone is the One whom we put on, and He covers us; we enter into Him and are sheltered; we hold His cross like a strong bow that never fails; our feet are strengthened so that we walk the way of truth, and we have the possibility of setting out not by a horse but by a heavenly chariot, and our heart is strengthened by Him, so that the day of the Lord is turned into a day of joy and victory. Our Jesus alone is our strength, our victory, our spiritual weapon, our eternal garment, our glory and our joy that is not taken away from us.

2.7.7.en: In ancient times the work of the Law was to declare the futility of all our human possibilities for salvation, not that we might live crushed, but that we might receive our Christ as the true source of our salvation.

2.7.8.en: The psalmist looked at those around him, hoping he might find help in the princes, but he realized their weakness, for he says: "Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help. His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth" (Ps 146:3). In bitterness he found no possibility of salvation even in his parents: "When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up" (Ps 27:10). And since he found no helper in all mankind, he said: "I said in my haste, All men are liars" (Ps 116:10). And if a man thinks himself mighty or a man of abilities, the Lord rebukes him: "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches" (Jer 9:23). And if he relies on his horse, he hears: "An horse is a vain thing for safety" (Ps 33:17); "But ye said, No; for we will flee upon horses; therefore shall ye flee: and, We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift" (Isa 30:16).

2.7.9.en: Therefore let us accept God Himself as our Savior, our wisdom, our riches, our strength, and everything to us!
